info.title: Tico API (v2)
info.description: The stable API for building your own frontend on Tico. Everything here keeps its shape within v2: fields are added, never removed or renamed, and a breaking change is a new /api/v3. Routes not listed are internal. Public roadmap writes require an allowlisted Origin; reads permit server-side requests. No sign-in or idempotency key (docs/roadmaps.md). Granola connection and sync writes do not require an idempotency key, nor does POST /api/v2/inbound/tasks, whose own `key` is its idempotency. Inbox company connection actions reconcile the same short-lived code under current grant checks. Other writes need an `Idempotency-Key` header (1-200 characters; a retry with the same key and body returns the first answer). Errors are `{"error": {code, detail, retryable}}`. See docs/custom-frontend.md.

Server-sent events: tasks, messages, runs, bots and Needs you as they change. topics=<comma list> (default all), after=<change number> resumes, conversation=<ids> narrows messages and runs, bot=<slugs> narrows runs and bots, task=<ids> and party=<actors> narrow tasks to those and to the ones those actors own or asked for, needs=changes sends Needs you as changed ids

200.description:
text/event-stream. Each change is `id: <change number>`, `event: <topic>` and JSON `data` with `seq`, `actor` (who made it, when the viewer may know) and `at`:
- `tasks`: `id` and `task` (as `GET /api/v2/tasks` shows it to the viewer), or `gone: true` for a deleted task.
- `messages`: `id`, `conversation_id` and `message` (as a conversation page shows it), or `deleted: true`; a chat goal set, paused, met or stopped is `goal_id` and `goal`.
- `runs`: `attempt_id`, `conversation_id`, `bot`, and either `output` (one step of the run: `kind`, `payload`) or `state` (`job_id`, and the job's or attempt's state).
- `bots`: `bot` and `status` (as `GET /api/v2/status` lists it).
- `needs`: the viewer's own Needs-you `count` and `items` (as `GET /api/v2/needs-you`), whenever anything on it may have moved. With `needs=changes`: `count`, `version`, each bot's count (`bots`), and the ids `changed` and `removed` since `base` (null when more than 100 moved: read the list whole); read the changed items with `GET /api/v2/needs-you?ids=`, and the whole list (or its first pages) when the version held is not `base`. `ready` then carries `needs_version`.
Also `event: ready` (`seq`: where the log stands), `event: cursor` (the change number to resume from, past changes the viewer may not see), `event: reset` (the client was further behind than the log keeps, 24 hours or more than 5,000 changes: read in full), `event: expired` (sign-in no longer valid; sign in and reconnect), and a `: keepalive` comment every 15 seconds. Only what the viewer may read is sent. A stream ends after about fifteen minutes; reconnect with `after` (or the browser's own `Last-Event-ID`). People only: a bot is refused with 403.

GroupMembers.description: Teammates of a group: humans by id, bots by slug.

GroupUpdate.title: GroupUpdate
GroupUpdate.description:
Rename a group, move it under another (`parent`; "" = top level), and add or remove teammates. A teammate
added to a group leaves the one it was in.

storage.description: Read-only file storage usage and copy progress; Team owners only

stuck.description: Bots with queued work that is not starting, or left in setup for over a day (the caller may read them): bot, name, queued, oldest, computer, reason (not_ready, computer_offline, no_computer, slow, limit, updating, restarting, setup, or a reason the claim holds the work: draining, maintaining, lane_held, uncertain, scoped, bot_limit, cooling_off, run_hold, budget, backoff, readiness_unknown, sign_in_rejected, not_isolated, isolation_unknown, profile, config, check_model, unreadable), why, drain_progress (counts of running and handed-back turns on update holds), since (setup only: when the bot was added), and fix (label plus href/tab, login, move or finish; null unless the caller administers bots, or for setup may manage the bot: finish is POST /api/v2/bots/{bot}/onboarded)

on_fallback.description: Bots whose latest run in the last day ran on a fallback harness (the caller may read them): bot, harness, since (when the unbroken run of fallback turns began)

limited.description: Bots a usage limit holds now (the caller may read them): bot, since

IfNoAnswer.title: IfNoAnswer
IfNoAnswer.description:
What the bot does if the person does not answer by `by` (backend/ask_deadlines.py). `kind` says what that step is:
only a `reversible` internal step goes ahead on its own; a send, a payment or a delete waits for an answer.

InboundTask.title: InboundTask
InboundTask.description:
What one piece of another system's work should look like now (POST /api/v2/inbound/tasks).
`owner`, `title` and `body` are needed only when the call files the task; anything left out
stays as it is.

id.description: A UUID, or auto:<bot>:<metric> for a bot's automatic KPI

freshness.description: stale: one period missed; missing: never read or two missed. archived: a retained goal link, not counting. Never zero

status.description: Against the target on the link (or a range); gray is stale or missing data; none is fresh with no target; null is an archived goal link with no colour

expected.description: Where the straight line from baseline to target is now

items.description: version, ts, actor, name, definition, unit, direction, cadence, source_note; newest first

superseded_by.description: The reading that corrected this one, if any

LibrarianResearch.title: LibrarianResearch
LibrarianResearch.description: A person asks the Librarian to research and add to one page (docs/librarian.md#research).

pins.description: Where the file is pinned, when pins exist

LocalFinding.title: LocalFinding
LocalFinding.description: A process the bot's watcher saw busy on its computer: a name and two numbers, never free text.

cost_usd.description: Filing-ledger list-price estimate, including subscription usage.

diff.description: Checked unified diff; present on detail reads and decisions, omitted from lists.

from_name.description: Display name of from_actor, when it is a person or a bot

body_raw.description: A notice Tico wrote, as stored (with actor ids); `body` shows names to people

edited_at.description: When the author last changed a task comment's text; null when never edited

deleted_at.description: When the author deleted a task comment. A delete or retry acknowledgment can include a tombstone with an empty body; deleted comments are never listed

run.description: The run that handled this message, once one has: on a person's message `{job_id, attempt_id, state}` where `state` is `started_run` (it started the run) or `added_to_run` (it was folded into a run already working); on a bot's reply `{job_id, attempt_id}` (the run that wrote it, plus a summary of what it did). Absent until a run takes the message

answers.description: On a structured ask: all review answers, oldest first. On a bot reply: handled message ids

woke.description: On a send: false when the message was held (see `held`)

held.description: On a send: a bot's message to a bot held for that bot's next run, and how to wake it now (backend/bot_to_bot.py)

sent_as.description: On a send to a bot: the way it went (steer, queue or defer) and a defer's deadline (backend/delivery.py)

actors.description: On reads: display names for every actor id in the answer, {"human:ana": "Ana Alvarez"}

older.description: Tasks there only for a question older than three days, out of the queue and its count

went_away.description: Items that left the caller's queue this week on their own: expired, withdrawn, answered by their Assistant, and the total

count.description: Items in the whole list, whatever page this is

next.description: With limit or cursor: pass as cursor for the next page; null on the last page

bots.description: With limit or cursor: how many items in the whole list each bot is behind

restart.description: The cursor was from an older version: this page is the first

OnboardingComplete.title: OnboardingComplete
OnboardingComplete.description: Mark onboarding complete (a person above the bot), or the bot's own "I'm ready" with what it learned.

stage.description: Onboarding (learns only: no tasks, routines or sends) until a person above it marks onboarding complete, then active

as_of.description: The date the data is from (YYYY-MM-DD)

stale_days.description: Days since the last version once past 1.5x the cadence; null while current or without a cadence

replaced_by.description: The newer page's file id, when the reader may see it

src.description: Where to frame the page; null means open it (GET /api/v2/files/{fid}/versions/{number})

pinned.description: The places it is pinned that the caller may open

PersonalTokenCreate.title: PersonalTokenCreate
PersonalTokenCreate.description:
A personal API token (backend/personal_tokens.py): a label to tell it apart in the list
and how long it lives; 90 days unless asked, never more than a year.

audience.description: A team page: who sees it (docs/permissions.md)

sign_in.description: On a 401 with built-in sign-in: the login path

questions.description: Keyed by question id, in judge.py's format

task_model.description: For a turn in a task's own session on a bot with a task model: `source` is task (it ran on the task model), fallback (the task model could not run, so the bot's own model did) or check (a check subtask kept its check model), and `note` says it in plain words

fallback.description: The fallback harness that ran the turn, if any

family.description: The maker of the model that did the work, from the model catalog, when every counted segment agrees; null is unknown (mixed, Cursor auto, OpenRouter, an unlisted model, nothing counted). Never the bot's configured model.

ReleaseBot.title: ReleaseBot
ReleaseBot.description: Release a bot from every hold Tico put on it (failed runs, run budget, queued runs it could not start).

ReportOrder.title: ReportOrder
ReportOrder.description:
A manager's direct reports in the order the team chart shows them: bot slugs and human ids (`bot:` or `human:`
in front when one could be either). Reports left out keep their places.

RuleCite.title: RuleCite
RuleCite.description:
The part of a document a rule rests on: a Files version (`file_id`, `version`; the current one by default), the
section it is in, and the quote, which must appear in that version's text (backend/counsel.py `check_cite`).

turns_at_once.title: Turns At Once
turns_at_once.description: Most turns this computer runs at once. Null is automatic: its own capacity.

ScreeningModes.title: ScreeningModes
ScreeningModes.description: A mode per source and a switch per detector; only what is sent changes.

SeatBatchCreate.title: SeatBatchCreate
SeatBatchCreate.description: A single confirmed group of Recruiting seats.

SeatCreate.title: SeatCreate
SeatCreate.description: A Recruiting seat: a role on the org chart with its job description and reporting line, and no bot.

SeatDraft.title: SeatDraft
SeatDraft.description: A job description for a seat not posted yet, drafted from its title (backend/recruiting.py `draft`).

SeatHire.title: SeatHire
SeatHire.description:
The candidate picked for a seat: a Tico template, on its suggested model unless `model` names another, named
after the seat unless `name` says otherwise, and on `runner_id`'s computer when one is chosen.

ServiceKeyCreate.title: ServiceKeyCreate
ServiceKeyCreate.description:
A service key (backend/service_keys.py): the label names the system that holds it, on every
task it files. `tasks` files tasks; `update` checks for, starts and follows an update of this install.

execution.description: The latest run: state, label, text (the reply so far; separate messages are joined by a blank line), parts, bot

StaleAcceptAll.title: StaleAcceptAll
StaleAcceptAll.description:
Accept all on a Stale tickets card: the rows the card showed, each with its task's version then. A row added
since is not in the list and stays; a row whose task changed is refused on its own.

StaleDecision.title: StaleDecision
StaleDecision.description:
A person's answer to one row of their Stale tickets card (backend/stale_review.py): accept or skip. Accept names
the task version the row showed (409 version_conflict once the task changed), as a change by hand does.

proposal_task.description: The owner's Needs you item, when filed

undo.description: What Undo restored and what it kept: {restored, kept, text}

task.description: The merged item: the Strategy Bot's task, waiting on the person

regular_checks.description: Whether the KPI pass and the automatic goal colours run

level_chosen.description: Whether the owner chose the level; if not, it is the default

asked_today.description: {person actor: items the Strategy Bot put in their Needs you today (UTC)}

StrategyDraftFrom.title: StrategyDraftFrom
StrategyDraftFrom.description: Setup's research job: the team's website, the owner's own words, or both (backend/strategy_setup.py).

SubscriptionWrite.title: SubscriptionWrite
SubscriptionWrite.description:
A new subscription, or a saved one's reconnect (a new `secret`) or rename. `confirm` accepts that a reconnect
stops and restarts the live runs on every computer given it.

SystemRoutineUpdate.title: SystemRoutineUpdate
SystemRoutineUpdate.description:
One system routine's switch, schedule preset or daily time (backend/system_routines.py); only what is sent
changes.

body.description: Left out of a list asked for with brief=true, as is acceptance_criteria

occurrence.description: A due-date routine's occurrence, "<automation_id>:<due_on>", on the task it opened: the due is its deadline, not a wake date.

owner_name.description: Display name of owner (`owner` stays the actor id)

open_asks.description: Questions on this task with no answer or dismissal

step_since.description: A Dev ticket at a working step (In Progress, a Fixes step): when it entered that step or came back to work; absent otherwise

relations.description: Related tasks the reader may open, by kind (parent, blocks, related, duplicate_of, follow_up): each {id, title, status, owner, direction}; direction is out when this task is the subtask, blocker, duplicate or follow-up, in for the other end, both for related. Subtasks are in the task's children.

number.description: The task's number, unique across the team (#18945); given once on a numbered type and never changed

step_rank.description: Its place within its step, lower first

waiting_on.description: The person a waiting task waits on; the task is in their Needs you

guest.description: The one person a private task with no person on it reached: its owning bot's first subtask, question or wait for them made them its guest. They read the task as its requester and owner do, and nothing else of its tree

snoozed_until.description: Set aside until this moment (UTC): off lists and Needs you, and quiet, until then

snoozed_note.description: What to check when the snooze ends (sent in the owner's wake)

roles.description: Who is on the task, by role: each role a short name the team chooses (developer, reviewer, qa ...) with its actors in the order they were added; a role nobody holds is absent, and one actor may hold several roles. Tico gives roles no meaning or rights. Task update and create take the same shape to replace a role's people ([] clears one)

public_summary.description: Separate public text; omitted with brief=true

TaskBlocker.title: TaskBlocker
TaskBlocker.description: What refused: an ask about the same repo, status and endpoint as an open one joins it (backend/blocker_asks.py).

TaskBulk.title: TaskBulk
TaskBulk.description:
One change to every task `filter` selects (`POST /api/v2/task-bulk`): `action` names it and its one field
carries the value: `step` (id or name), `status`, `owner`, `add` or `remove` (tags, for `tags`), or none for
`close`. `note` goes with each task's change, as on a single update.

TaskCap.title: TaskCap
TaskCap.description: A cap on the tasks `sender` sends `receiver` a day. null (or left out) removes it; 0 blocks the pair.

actors.description: On reads: display names for every actor id in the answer, {"human:ana": "Ana Alvarez"}

TaskFilter.title: TaskFilter
TaskFilter.description: The tasks a bulk change applies to: the filters `GET /api/v2/tasks` takes, with the same meanings.

cursor.description: Opaque: pass as changed_after to read only what changed since

gone.description: With changed_after: ids that changed and no longer match (deleted, no longer readable, or out of the filters)

reset.description: With changed_after: the cursor is too old or no longer applies; read in full

actors.description: On reads: display names for every actor id in the answer, {"human:ana": "Ana Alvarez"}

TaskRelation.title: TaskRelation
TaskRelation.description:
`{id} kind {task}`: parent (task is its parent), blocks, blocked_by, related, duplicate_of,
follow_up (it was split off or followed up from task).

TaskRelationRef.title: TaskRelationRef
TaskRelationRef.description: The new task `kind` the other: `parent` files it under `task`, `blocked_by` makes it wait on it.

model.title: Model
model.description: The model the task's runs use; null clears the task's choice

TaskRunModel.title: TaskRunModel
TaskRunModel.description:
A task's own model (backend/task_run_models.py). An absent `model` keeps the task's and changes only the
effort or harness named; a null `model` clears it, so the task's runs use the bot's task model again.

flow.description: What the step does with a ticket (docs/tasks.md, Step flow). On a check step, other_company is prefer (the default) or require.

flow.title: Flow
flow.description: The step's flow (docs/tasks.md, Step flow). On a check step, other_company is prefer (the default) or require.

bots.description: What every bot may do with the type's tasks beyond its own: read (read, comment, file subtasks) or work (also change them); null keeps each task to the bots on it

role.description: The Product roadmap or Dev tickets type, whoever manages it

TeamBudgets.title: TeamBudgets
TeamBudgets.description: The team defaults for bots with no budget of their own. Fields left out stay as they are; 0 is no limit.

TeammateAccess.title: TeammateAccess
TeammateAccess.description:
A person's or a group's See, Read and Write (backend/teammate_access.py), in a bot's shape. `revision` is the
one the editor read: 0 while they still have the defaults.

sub_thread.description: The sub-thread branching from this message: {id, count, last_seq, unread, more}

retention_days.description: Days a root keeps its messages; null keeps them for good

ToolRegister.title: ToolRegister
ToolRegister.description:
A tool a person registers for a bot (backend/bot_tools.py). Names and verbs only: `env` is the
variable's name, and the server refuses a field that looks like a credential.

ToolUpdate.title: ToolUpdate
ToolUpdate.description:
A change to a tool a bot already declares (backend/bot_tools.py): only what is sent changes. `scope` keys
are set one by one (an empty value takes a key off); `note` "" clears the note.

TriggerSigning.title: TriggerSigning
TriggerSigning.description:
`secret` the sender was given (GitHub lets you type one); empty makes a new one. `preset` says how calls are
checked (hmac, github, standard, stripe, slack; the current one, else hmac, when empty). `off` stops checking.

TriggerUpdate.title: TriggerUpdate
TriggerUpdate.description: Any of these; what is left out stays. `type_from` empty goes back to the preset's default.

meetings_pending.description: Pending meetings filed for the caller; never part of Needs you

prices_as_of.description: The date the price table was read

items.description: By bot: bot, name, department; by day: day; by routine: routine (null for runs that came from none), title, bot, name. Every row has the usage figures and `share`, its part of the total (estimate plus API-equivalent)

dimensions.description: Available dimension filters, scoped to visible runs

dimension_labels.description: Display labels keyed by immutable filter value; subscription names include their Computer

cached_tokens.description: Input tokens read from the provider's cache

est_cost_usd.description: List-price estimate for runs billed by API key; null when every such run used a model with no list price

subscription_equiv_usd.description: What runs on a ChatGPT or Claude sign-in would cost through the API: not money spent, never added to est_cost_usd

unpriced_runs.description: Runs with tokens on a model with no list price

low_estimate_runs.description: Priced runs whose estimate may be low: the model charges more for long prompts and the runner did not report every request's tokens

source.description: Where each cap comes from: bot, company or null

percent.description: The highest share of one of the bot's own limits reached

blocked.description: Set while a limit is met, the bot's own, a pool's or a Finance budget's (quarterly, yearly, or budget for a one-time budget): the bot takes no new job

blocked_by.description: Whose limit holds the bot: scope (bot, company, group:<id> or budget), name (a pool's or budget's), period, until for a budget ("" when it never turns over), and spent and limit (a pool's to the owner and administrators only)

pools.description: Owner and administrators: company (UsagePoolView) and groups, {id: UsagePoolView with name and parent}. A lead who is not an administrator: company null and only the groups it leads and those below, each with may_edit true

VisualRef.title: VisualRef
VisualRef.description: A file version attached to a message with the title it shows under (backend/visuals.py).

filter.description: departments, bots, task_types; an empty list means all

items.description: name, secret, and value unless secret (then set: true)

webhook.description: With `secret` once; `replayed: true` on a retry, without it

bearer.description: A bearer session from POST /auth/token (browser apps) or a personal API token (servers).

serviceKey.description: A service key, tico_sk_...: a tasks key reaches POST /api/v2/inbound/tasks and nothing else (an update key reaches only /api/v2/system/update, docs/service-keys.md).

cookie.name: tico_session
cookie.description: The browser session of Tico's own page (`__Host-tico_session` over https).
